item.title: Court Rejects Atiku’s Bid to Tender Fresh Evidence In Suit Seeking Tinubu’s Disqualification
item.description: Justice Inyang Ekwo of the Federal High Court in Abuja has dismissed an application by former Vice President and the African Democratic Congress (ADC) presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, to present fresh evidence in his suit seeking to prevent President Bola Tinubu from contesting the 2027 presidential election over allegations of forgery of his National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) discharge certificate. The judge held that the time allowed by law to present evidence in a pre-election suit was 14 days, in line with Section 285(9) of the 1999 Constitution. Justice Ekwo agreed with Tinubu and the other defendants that allowing Atiku to introduce fresh evidence would alter the nature of the original case and violate the provisions of the Constitution. In his ruling on Atiku’s application to amend the originating summons in the suit against Tinubu, the All Progressives Congress (APC) and the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), the judge held that the former vice president attempted to mislead the court by claiming that the proposed amendment would not introduce fresh issues. Justice Ekwo said that, after carefully examining the application, the court found that the ADC presidential candidate sought to substitute existing evidence with new evidence which, if allowed, would circumvent Section 285(9) of the Constitution, which requires such evidence to be presented within 14 days. A man walks past the Federal High Court premises in Abuja, on April 22, 2026. (Photo by LIGHT ORIYE TAMUNOTONYE / AFP) According to the judge, allowing Atiku to introduce fresh evidence through the back door would amount to a fundamental injustice against the defendants. Meanwhile, following an agreement among the lawyers, the judge fixed December 2 for the hearing of the substantive suit. Atiku had told the court that he needed to make substantial amendments to his case challenging Tinubu’s eligibility to participate in the 2027 presidential election. In the main suit, Atiku and the ADC asked Justice Ekwo to disqualify Tinubu and the APC from the 2027 presidential election. They challenged the authenticity of Tinubu’s NYSC discharge certificate submitted to INEC by the APC. The plaintiffs, who sued the president, the APC and INEC as the first to third defendants, respectively, in an originating summons marked FHC/ABJ/CS/1888/2026, alleged that the APC submitted a forged NYSC discharge certificate belonging to the president to INEC. INEC Headquarters in Abuja. They, therefore, asked the court to compel INEC to remove Tinubu’s name and that of the APC from the list of candidates and political parties for the presidential election. However, Tinubu and the APC, in a joint counter-affidavit filed on September 9, urged the court to dismiss the suit in its entirety for being incompetent, arguing that the plaintiffs lacked the legal right to institute the case. item.title: ‘That’s Not What’s Driving Me’: Tonye Cole Denies Trading Support For Future APC Governorship Ticket
item.description: Former Rivers State governorship candidate of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Tonye Cole, has denied that his decision to support the party’s political arrangement ahead of the 2027 elections was motivated by a promise of a future governorship ticket. Cole said his priority was to change the perception of Rivers State as a place associated with violence and political strongmen, arguing that peace and security were essential to attracting investment to the state. He spoke on Friday while appearing as a guest on Channels Television’s The Morning Brief , where he was asked whether he had been promised an opportunity to pursue his governorship ambition in the future. “No, and that is not what is driving me,” he replied. “What is driving me is that if you cannot bring peace and security and change the narrative of Rivers State, investment will not come to Rivers State. So the first aspect of it is that we must change the mindset of everyone that when they talk about Rivers State, violence, strongman, no gentlemen, loud, all of that tagline must change. “If I cannot be the face of what the future of Rivers State politics should look like, then we have a problem,” he added. ﻿ Cole, who emerged as the APC governorship candidate in 2019 and 2023, withdrew from the party’s 2027 governorship race in May following consultations and efforts to reconcile rival factions within the state chapter. He subsequently aligned with the Rainbow Coalition, a cross-party political arrangement led by the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Nyesom Wike, which is backing President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid. Explaining his decision to remain with the APC group that predated the current political arrangement, Cole said he wanted to ensure that members who had worked to build the party were not sidelined. “For me, abandoning those who were in APC who worked was not the question. So I decided that I was going to stay with them so that they would have a voice. They cannot be removed, so I stayed there to represent the voice of the APC that built forth and kept Rivers State whole,” he said. He added that the decision to bring different political interests together was informed by the need to prevent divisions that had previously weakened the APC in Rivers State. ‘No Differences With Wike’ A combo of Cole, Wike, and logos of the APC and PDP Wike holds near-total control over the formal political institutions and party structures in Rivers State. There was intense, public friction and even a defamation lawsuit between Cole and the FCT minister before they reconciled to form the Rainbow Coalition. Cole, speaking further, said he and Wike had put their past disagreements behind them and were now working towards a common political objective. “I believe politics is about sacrifice. There is no politician who does not have scars. But you have to be looking at the future. So today, Nyesom Wike and I do not have any differences. “What was in the past was in the past.

item.title: Stop recycling falsehoods against Tinubu, Lagos APC tells Pearse
item.description: By Olasunkanmi Akoni The Lagos State chapter of the All Progressives Congress (APC) has slammed Dr. Adetokunbo Pearse over his recent series of interviews allegedly maligning and disparaging President Bola Ahmed Tinubu. Lagos State APC Spokesman, Seye Oladejo, who made the remark, described the statement as “an obsessive campaign of calumny,” against the President. The party said it would ordinarily have ignored the outbursts as a desperate attempt by a politically stranded individual to remain relevant, but added that the frequency, desperation and recycled nature of the allegations made it necessary to set the records straight. “There is something particularly unfortunate about a man who appears incapable of moving beyond yesterday’s political arguments, even when the issues he continues to resurrect have been exhaustively examined, contested and addressed through established legal and judicial processes,” the party stated. The APC said repetition does not transform an allegation into evidence, neither does the frequency with which a falsehood is circulated confer credibility upon it. “The Nigerian public is not obliged to accept recycled accusations simply because they are delivered with theatrical confidence in television studios,” it said. The party questioned how Pearse’s purported knowledge of the President’s academic history could be conclusive when, by his own account, he served at Chicago State University between 1985 and 1990, whereas President Tinubu’s academic records establish that he attended the institution between 1977 and 1979. “How does a lecturer who arrived at an institution six years after a student’s graduation become the ultimate authority on whether that student ever attended the institution?” the party asked. It described the discrepancy as not minor, saying “it goes to the very foundation of his latest claims,” adding that one would expect an academic of his purported standing to appreciate the importance of chronology, documentary evidence and elementary standards of verification. The party noted that the Chicago State University controversy is not a matter left to speculation, as the university itself has repeatedly confirmed President Tinubu’s attendance and graduation in 1979. It recalled that its Registrar, Caleb Westberg, also testified under oath in October 2023, confirming that the university’s official academic records showed that Bola Ahmed Tinubu graduated on June 22, 1979, with a degree in Business Administration. “These were not whispers in political corridors or claims made by hired political communicators. They were official institutional records and sworn testimony produced in the course of proceedings initiated at the instance of former Vice President Atiku Abubakar,” the party said. item.title: Uche Nnaji: HURIWA accuses ICPC of political persecution, demands halt to prosecution
item.description: … Alleges plot to weaken Mbah’s political challenger … Warns against weaponising anti-graft agencies ahead of 2027 elections By Chioma Obinna The Human Rights Writers Association of Nigeria (HURIWA) on Friday accused the Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission (ICPC) of using its prosecution of former Minister of Science, Technology and Innovation, Uche Nnaji, to advance political interests in Enugu State, demanding an immediate halt to the case pending an independent review. The rights group alleged that the continued prosecution of Nnaji, amid the controversy surrounding his academic qualifications, raises serious questions about the neutrality and independence of the anti-corruption agency, particularly as political activities gather momentum ahead of the 2027 general elections. In a press statement signed by its National Coordinator, Comrade Emmanuel Nnadozie Onwubiko, HURIWA warned that criminal prosecution must not become an instrument for intimidating opposition figures, weakening political challengers or protecting incumbent office holders. The association alleged that Nnaji’s prosecution increasingly bears the appearance of a political project designed to undermine one of the formidable challengers to Enugu State Governor, Peter Mbah. It claimed that the former minister remains one of the few politicians capable of mounting a serious challenge to Mbah’s political dominance, raising concerns that state institutions could be deployed to influence the state’s political landscape. HURIWA said: “The ICPC must stop this prosecution if it cannot convincingly establish that the process is independent, evidence-driven and free from political considerations. Nigerians must not allow persecution to disguise itself as prosecution.” The group maintained that while allegations against Nnaji should be subjected to lawful investigation and accountability, they must not provide a justification for selective deployment of state institutions against political actors. It also recalled that Nnaji had approached the Federal High Court to compel the University of Nigeria, Nsukka, to release his academic transcript, noting that the controversy surrounding his academic records remained contentious. According to HURIWA, the circumstances surrounding the investigation and prosecution require closer scrutiny to ensure that the anti-corruption agency is not acting on political considerations. The association further accused the Federal Government of failing to prevent anti-corruption institutions from operating in ways that could intimidate perceived political opponents and distort the country’s multiparty democratic process. Invoking the democratic principles underpinning the Electoral Act 2022, HURIWA argued that political competition must be free from intimidation, coercion and abuse of institutional power. item.title: ‎INEC releases 86,931 new PVCs for collection in Kogi
item.description: ‎By Boluwaji Obahopo, Lokoja ‎‎The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) in Kogi State has announced the availability of 86,931 Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs) for residents who participated in the second phase of the Continuous Voter Registration (CVR) exercise. ‎The State Resident Electoral Commissioner (REC) Dr. Shehu Wahab, made this known in a press statement made available to newsmen in Lokoja on Friday. ‎According to the commission, the second phase of the CVR exercise was conducted between January 5 and April 17, 2026. ‎‎INEC said, “The 86,931 PVCs produced for eligible registrants have been delivered to our offices across the 21 Local Government Areas of the state and are now ready for collection.” ‎‎The commission advised registrants to visit the INEC office in the Local Government Area where they completed their registration to collect their cards. ‎‎It said registrants are expected to come with their registration slips or printouts, or a valid means of identification where required. ‎‎INEC also clarified that PVCs from the first phase of the registration exercise are still available for collection. ‎‎”PVCs would not be issued through proxies, registrants must personally collect their cards. Collection is available at INEC LGA offices from 9:00 a.m. to 3:00 p.m., Monday to Friday.” ‎The commission further directed registrants to check the status of their PVCs and locate their collection centres through its CVR portal, cvr.inecnigeria.org. ‎‎INEC urged all voters who participated in the second phase of the CVR exercise to collect their PVCs without delay, noting that the cards are essential for participation in future elections. ‎‎The commission said timely collection would help ensure that no eligible voter is disenfranchised. ‎‎Wahab expressed appreciation to registrants for their patience during the production, verification and distribution processes, assuring that the commission remained committed to ensuring that every eligible voter obtains a PVC and is able to exercise their democratic right. The post ‎INEC releases 86,931 new PVCs for collection in Kogi appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: 2030: FG takes decisive action to end open defecation with Executive Order
item.description: By Gabriel Ewepu ABUJA – IN a renewed commitment, the Federal Government has unveiled a new Executive Order to accelerate Nigeria’s drive towards ending open defecation by 2030. The unveiling of the Open Defecation Free Nigeria by 2030 and Other Related Matters Order, 2025 coincided with the commemoration of World Toilet Day and the seventh anniversary of the Clean Nigeria campaign in Abuja on Thursday. Vice President Kashim Shettima, represented by the Senior Special Assistant to the President on Delivery and Coordination in the Office of the Vice President, Akubo Adegbe, described the Executive Order as a decisive step towards translating government commitments into measurable sanitation outcomes. Shettima said the order marks a transition from fragmented interventions to stronger coordination, measurable results and sustainable national progress. He called on state and local governments to strengthen accountability, increase sanitation financing and sustain community-led behavioural change He disclosed that since the launch of the Clean Nigeria campaign in 2019, 185 of the country’s 774 local government areas have attained Open Defecation Free (ODF) status, while Jigawa and Katsina remain the only states certified as ODF nationwide. While acknowledging the progress recorded, the Vice President warned that the country still had considerable ground to cover, urging states yet to achieve ODF status to establish monthly and quarterly targets and make their progress publicly available. He also cautioned against a reversal of gains in communities already certified as open defecation-free, stressing the need for sustained monitoring and accountability to protect existing achievements. According to him, Nigeria must prioritise sustainable financing, reliable data, stronger institutions, effective implementation and continuous behavioural change to achieve the 2030 target. He also called on state and local governments to take ownership of the campaign by allocating adequate resources and strengthening sanitation institutions, while urging development partners, the private sector, traditional rulers, community leaders and civil society organisations to sustain their support. Shettima, who chairs the Steering Committee of the Clean Nigeria Project, reaffirmed the Federal Government’s commitment to working with subnational governments, noting that the National Economic Council would also be deployed to advance and sustain the national sanitation agenda. Linking the campaign to this year’s World Toilet Day theme, “Sanitation and Gender Equality,” the Vice President highlighted the disproportionate burden poor sanitation places on women and girls. He noted that inadequate access to safe and private sanitation facilities undermines their health, security, dignity, education and participation in economic and social activities. item.title: ‘There Are People Telling Tinubu Lies About Nigerians’ Support,’ Says Baba-Ahmed
item.description: The National Chairman of the Peoples Redemption Party (PRP), Hakeem Baba-Ahmed, has accused some political loyalists of misleading President Bola Tinubu about the level of public support for his administration. Baba-Ahmed, who once served under the Tinubu administration as Special Adviser on Political Matters in the Office of the Vice President, said the president’s associates could be giving him a false impression of his popularity by relying on assurances from governors and party loyalists rather than listening to ordinary Nigerians. He made the remarks on Friday during an appearance on Channels Television’s The Morning Brief programme. The PRP chairman said his assessment of public sentiment was based on his grassroots political connections and familiarity with the administration, which he initially supported. “I’m a politician. I lead a political party that is entirely grassroots-based. I have very strong organic links with the people. I followed the Tinubu administration from inception. Initially, I was even part of it,” he said. ﻿ Baba-Ahmed said he was familiar with the feelings of Nigerians and was not exaggerating the widespread dissatisfaction with the government. He identified poverty, economic mismanagement, corruption and insecurity as some of the issues contributing to the growing distance between the administration and the people. He also suggested that some political associates were giving Tinubu assurances about his chances of securing re-election in 2027 without adequately reflecting the mood of Nigerians. “There are a lot of people who are telling President Tinubu lies if he thinks himself, and they think that the people are with them. Just look at wherever APC goes. People either chase them away or they trigger violence,” he said. ‘Bamayi’ Baba-Ahmed also described the ‘Bamayi’ chants directed at the president as an expression of widespread dissatisfaction, insisting that the sentiment was not restricted to young people or northern Nigerians. “This Bamayi thing, it’s not just a slogan that young people throw at APC. It’s genuinely an organic element of the way Nigerians, not just northerners, Nigerians feel,” he added. The ‘Bamayi’ chants, which translate to ‘we don’t want’ in Hausa, were heard on November 13 after Tinubu attended Friday prayers at the Shehu Shagari Mosque in the Garki area of Abuja. Some protesters reportedly threw stones at the president’s convoy and destroyed APC campaign posters, prompting security operatives to intervene. The incident attracted reactions from political figures, including Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) chieftain Segun Sowunmi, who condemned the protesters’ actions. Sowunmi, who is also a member of the APC campaign council, criticised the destruction of campaign posters and the use of violence during an appearance on Channels Television’s *Politics Today* on Monday. item.title: Dollar to Naira exchange rate today, November 20, 2026
item.description: The Nigerian naira continued to face downward pressure against the United States dollar across both the official Nigerian Foreign Exchange Market (NFEM) and the parallel market on Friday, November 20, 2026, driven by tightening foreign exchange supply and rising end-of-year seasonal demand. Official Market Performance Real-time interbank spot tracking at the Nigerian Foreign Exchange Market placed the US dollar at ₦1,352.54 during early morning trading on Friday, following an opening rate of ₦1,351.86 and an intraday peak of ₦1,355.31. This early session trading follows Thursday’s official Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) volume-weighted benchmark, which saw the naira depreciate to a four-month low. According to official CBN data for the November 19 trading session, the NFEM weighted average rate settled at ₦1,376.58 per dollar, while the indicative closing rate rose to ₦1,388.00 per dollar from ₦1,379.99 recorded on Wednesday. Intraday interbank transactions on Thursday were conducted between a low of ₦1,370.00 and a high of ₦1,397.00 per dollar. Despite the depreciation, market liquidity improved significantly, with NFEM interbank turnover surging by 59.13 percent to $800.31 million across 184 deals, up from $502.88 million the previous day. Parallel Market Rates In the parallel market, commonly referred to as the black market, the local currency weakened further as Bureau de Change (BDC) operators and street dealers in Lagos and Abuja quoted the US dollar at a selling rate of up to ₦1,468 per dollar on Friday morning, following Thursday’s close between ₦1,461 and ₦1,468. Buying rates among informal currency dealers hovered between ₦1,445 and ₦1,458 depending on transaction volume and location. With Thursday’s official closing benchmark at ₦1,388.00 and parallel market quotations reaching ₦1,468.00, the spread between the official and unofficial windows widened to ₦80.00 per dollar, compared to ₦70.01 recorded earlier in the week. Market Drivers and Reserve Outlook Since the end of October, when the naira closed at ₦1,346.00 in the official window and ₦1,373.00 in the parallel market, the currency has lost ₦42.00 and ₦95.00 in the respective segments. Meanwhile, Nigeria’s gross external reserves stood at $54.71 billion as of November 18, 2026, reflecting a moderation of $554 million from the October 27 peak of $55.26 billion. Financial analysts note that the recent divergence between both windows is largely fueled by heightened festive import demand, corporate obligations, and reduced autonomous foreign exchange inflows rather than a structural depletion of the country’s external reserves. item.title: Why we pulled down Umeh’s billboard — Anambra govt
item.description: The Anambra State Government has dismissed claims that a billboard belonging to Senator Victor Umeh was pulled down because it carried the image of former Governor Peter Obi, calling the allegation false and misleading. The government said the enforcement action stemmed from an alleged violation of the Anambra State Signage Act, 2010, rather than the identity or political affiliation of anyone featured on the billboard. In a statement issued yesterday, the Commissioner for Information and Value Reformation, Dr Law Mefor, said that although Senator Umeh had paid the required signage fee, Peter Obi had not complied with the payment requirement. Mefor alleged that the senator, instead of fully complying with the law, used the billboard to promote the presidential candidate of the New Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), thereby contravening the state’s signage regulations. He stressed that the removal was carried out strictly in accordance with the law, which he noted was enacted during Peter Obi’s administration as governor of Anambra State. “For the avoidance of doubt, the billboard was not pulled down because of Peter Obi’s image,” the commissioner stated. The government further warned that any combined billboard campaign featuring candidates who had not fulfilled their signage obligations would face similar enforcement, regardless of their political party, status, or affiliation. It maintained that the state’s outdoor advertising regulations would be guided by fairness, transparency, and even-handed application of the law. Mefor urged the public to disregard what he described as a misleading narrative surrounding the incident, insisting that the government remained committed to due process and equal treatment in enforcing existing laws. item.title: ESUT to be renamed after Jim Nwobodo – Mbah
item.description: Governor of Enugu State, Dr. Peter Mbah, has unveiled plans to rename the Enugu State University of Science and Technology (ESUT) after a Second Republic Governor of old Anambra State, Senator Jim Nwobodo, subject to stakeholders engagement and legislative due process. Mbah made this known during the 3rd Distinguished Personality Lecture of the university delivered by Nwobodo at the Barr. Peter Ndubuisi Mbah Multipurpose Auditorium, ESUT, Enugu, on Thursday. He said the idea, which was first suggested by the ESUT Alumni Association, was in tandem with his thoughts, describing it as a fitting tribute to the elder statesman, who founded the institution in 1980. The Governor emphasised that the brainchild of the ex-governor had played a critical role in the human capital development of not just Enugu State, but also the old Anambra State and Nigeria as a whole. “Recently, representatives of the alumni of this university and its associated institutions came to see me. “They asked that Enugu State University of Science and Technology be renamed in honour of Senator Jim Ifeanyichukwu Nwobodo. “I told them that I support the proposal. I was particularly encouraged that the request came from the alumni who understand, through their own experience, what the university has meant to people’s lives. “There is a legal process to follow. ESUT was established by law, and changing its name would require the appropriate legislative steps and engagement with relevant stakeholders. “I intend to begin those engagements and work with the institutions concerned to advance the proposal through the proper process. “Your Excellency, I hope that gives you some sense of the regard in which your contribution continues to be held.” The Governor praised Nwobodo’s vision and courage in leadership, especially for investing heavily in human capital development, taking the bold step to establish ESUT a few years after the civil war, not minding the enormity of the challenges involved. “I have often wondered what it must have felt like to be governor in 1979. Nigeria had just returned to civilian government after thirteen years of military rule. “The Civil War had ended less than a decade earlier, and the country was still dealing with its consequences. There was much to rebuild, and enormous pressure on the resources available to government. “For many families, university education remained beyond their reach. And here was a young governor, who decided that his state should establish a university of science and technology. “People questioned whether it could be done. Was there enough money? Could a state government sustain such an institution? Shouldn’t this be left to the federal government? “These were reasonable questions. I suspect some of them would have kept you awake at night. “But for Jim Nwobodo, the fact that a problem is difficult does not mean we can afford to avoid it. “In July 1980, Anambra State University of Technology was established. item.title: Farmer allegedly macheted over grazing dispute in Benue
item.description: By Peter Duru, Makurdi A farmer, identified as Mr Terkura Orvanya, has reportedly been macheted by suspected herdsmen following a disagreement over the grazing of cattle on his cultivated farm at Ikpakena village, Makurdi Local Government Area of Benue State. Orvanya was said to have sustained serious machete wounds while attempting to defend himself against one of the herders after challenging them for allowing their cattle to destroy his melon farm. The incident was made public by Joseph Apahar, Media and Publicity Officer of IDP Benue State, in a social media post. According to Apahar, two herders were grazing their cattle on Orvanya’s melon farm when the farmer arrived and asked them to remove the animals from his cultivated crops. He alleged that the herders, despite being aware that the farm belonged to the farmer, showed no concern and refused to move the cattle away. Apahar said trouble started when Orvanya attempted to chase the animals out of his farm, prompting one of the herders to allegedly draw a cutlass and attack him. He said the farmer sustained machete wounds while attempting to shield himself from the attack, adding that Orvanya was receiving medical attention at a private hospital. Expressing concern over the incident, Apahar lamented what he described as the increasing cases of herders allowing their cattle to destroy cultivated crops, particularly farms containing crops ready for harvest or already harvested. He noted that such incidents were becoming increasingly common in the area, describing the development as a recurrence of the annual clashes between farmers and herders during harvest seasons after a period of relative peace. Apahar appealed to security agencies to urgently intervene to protect farmers and their investments from further destruction. “We are appealing to the security agencies to intervene urgently and help secure our crops before we are forced out of our villages, losing everything, and thereby reduced to nothing,” he said. He stressed that farmers should be allowed to harvest their crops without intimidation or attacks, insisting that their lives and livelihoods must be protected. “Our farmers deserve to harvest in peace. Our lives and livelihoods must be protected,” Apahar added. Efforts to reach the Police Public Relations Officer, DSP Peter Aondongu, for comments on the incident were unsuccessful, as he could not be reached at the time of filing this report. item.title: FG targets raw mineral export ban, revenue tops N100bn
item.description: By Gabriel Ewepu The Federal Government is pushing to end the export of unprocessed solid minerals as part of efforts to deepen local value addition, boost industrialisation and create jobs, even as revenue from the sector crossed N100 billion in 2026. President Bola Tinubu stated this yesterday at the Nigeria Now! Investing in Energy, Infrastructure and Mining Summit in Abuja, themed, “United Nigeria, New Horizons, One Investment Destination.” Tinubu said Nigeria was determined to move beyond exporting raw mineral resources, stressing the need for investment in processing and beneficiation to strengthen domestic industries. “In mining, we’re equally determined to move beyond the export of unprocessed resources. Better geological information, transparent licensing, responsible exploration, and greater investment in beneficiation and processing must support Nigerian industries, skilled employment and meaningful benefits for host communities,” he said. The President said the government was working to build integrated value chains that would enable Nigerian enterprises to participate more actively in the mining industry and expand domestic capabilities. He urged investors to bring technology, finance and commercial expertise, assuring them of efforts to strengthen regulatory certainty and institutional support for sustainable returns. Earlier, Minister of Solid Minerals Development, Dr Dele Alake, said reforms introduced by the Tinubu administration had increased revenue from the sector from N6 billion annually before the administration to N100 billion in 2026. “When I assumed office, the sector’s total annual revenue stood at just N6 billion. However, through reforms, the local value addition policy, the digitisation of mining processes, and efforts to sanitise operations within the sector, that figure increased from N6 billion to N38 billion by 2024. “By 2025, it had risen to N70 billion. And just about a week ago, the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) informed us that we had crossed the N100 billion mark this year,” Alake said. He attributed the growth to reforms and efforts to sanitise mining operations, including the establishment of Mining Marshals, which he said had apprehended over 300 illegal operators and recovered more than 100 mining sites. Meanwhile, Minister of Marine and Blue Economy, Gboyega Oyetola, said revenue generated by agencies under his ministry rose from N700.79 billion in 2023 to N1.83 trillion in 2025. He cited improvements in maritime security, port reforms and approval of Nigeria’s first National Policy on Marine and Blue Economy, while urging investors to explore opportunities in shipping, ports, shipbuilding, fisheries, aquaculture and logistics. item.title: Dollar scarcity, festive demand push Naira to N1,468/$
item.description: By Babajide Komolafe & Elizabeth Adegbesan The naira yesterday continued its downward trend in both segments of the foreign exchange market, depreciating to N1,468 per dollar in the parallel market from N1,450 per dollar on Wednesday, as dwindling dollar supply and rising demand ahead of the festive season intensified pressure on the currency. Similarly, the naira weakened to N1,388 per dollar in the Nigerian Foreign Exchange Market, NFEM, from N1,379.99 per dollar on Wednesday, representing a depreciation of N8.01. Data from the Central Bank of Nigeria, CBN, showed that the indicative exchange rate in the official market rose to N1,388 per dollar. Consequently, the gap between the parallel and official markets widened to N80 per dollar from N70.01 per dollar on Wednesday. Meanwhile, interbank turnover in the NFEM rose by 59.13 per cent to $800.3 million from $502.9 million recorded on Wednesday. Vanguard analysis showed that the naira has depreciated by N95 in the parallel market since October 31, when it closed at N1,373 per dollar. Similarly, the currency has depreciated by N42 in the official market from N1,346 per dollar at the end of October. The nation’s external reserves also declined to $54.71 billion on Wednesday, November 18, 2026, according to CBN data, representing a decline of $554 million from the peak of $55.264 billion recorded on October 27, 2026. Commenting on the development, Chief Investment Officer of VNL Capital Asset Management, Dr. Ubah Jeremiah, said the naira’s weakness was driven more by tightening dollar supply and rising seasonal demand than by significant depletion of external reserves. He said foreign exchange inflows had fallen sharply to about $807.6 million in the latest week from $2.48 billion previously, reducing dollar availability in the market. “With fewer dollars coming in from autonomous sources, the market has leaned more heavily on CBN supply just as importers, businesses, and individuals step up purchases ahead of the festive season and year-end obligations,” he said. Ubah also blamed diverging monetary policy positions between the CBN and the US Federal Reserve for reinforcing pressure on the naira, noting that higher US yields and a stronger dollar could weaken the attractiveness of naira assets and encourage portfolio outflows. Meanwhile, parallel-market trader, Jubril Yinusa, attributed the depreciation to rising demand and limited dollar supply. “The naira has recorded continuous depreciation this week due to the high demand as the festive season approaches and low supply. Importation demand is also contributing to the depreciation of the naira,” he said. Another trader, Isa Dauda, said the festive season and the forthcoming election were also contributing to pressure on the currency. He said some foreign investors were adopting a wait-and-see attitude ahead of the elections, further limiting foreign exchange inflows. item.title: Tinubu moves to achieve 40% fares reduction under NACTP
item.description: President Bola Tinubu in his determination to achieve the 40 percent fare-reduction target under the National Affordable CNG Transit Programme NACTP, as outlined in his renewed hope agenda 2.0, has welcomed plans by Yutong, the world’s largest bus manufacturer and a global leader in electric and CNG-powered buses, to establish a CNG bus assembly plant in Nigeria. This followed his invitation to the Chinese automotive giant to support the expansion of affordable mass transportation across the country. Special Adviser to the President on Information and Strategy, Mr. Bayo Onanuga, in a statement, yesterday, noted that the investment would support the National Affordable CNG Transit Programme, NACTP, in collaboration with state governments, which targets transport fare reductions of approximately 40 percent on participating routes, in line with the President’s renewed hope agenda 2.0 for 2027–2031. Under the agreement with the Presidential Initiative on Compressed Natural Gas and Electric Vehicles, Pi-CNG & EV, Yutong will supply an initial 300 CNG-powered buses, with the first 100 expected to arrive in Lagos by the end of December 2026. Subsequent buses will be assembled in Nigeria through YP Automobiles Bus Assembly at the former Leyland Automotive plant in Ibadan, Oyo State, reviving local industrial capacity, reducing dependence on imported vehicles and creating employment opportunities for Nigerian engineers, technicians and other workers. Yutong, which sold 49,518 buses globally in 2025, brings extensive experience in mass transit manufacturing, with operations across international markets and a track record of supporting local assembly and public transportation projects in several countries. The President noted that the investment comes as CNG adoption continues to increase nationwide, supported by the expansion of refuelling infrastructure through Pi-CNG & EV, the Midstream and Downstream Gas Infrastructure Fund, MDGIF, and private sector investors. These interventions include deploying Mobile Refuelling Units (MRUs) and the President’s directive for 2,000 additional CNG refuelling infrastructure units nationwide, laying the foundation for a wider rollout of affordable commercial buses. President Tinubu emphasises that reducing the daily cost of transportation for Nigerians remains the central objective of these investments. The President notes that millions of Nigerians depend on commercial transportation to get to work, take their children to school, travel to markets and move goods between communities. For many households, transportation consumes a significant portion of their daily earnings. He stresses that the lower operating costs of CNG-powered vehicles must translate into lower fares for passengers, allowing workers, traders and families to retain more of their income for food, education and other essential needs. item.title: ‘Obi Will Disgrace Him Spectacularly In Anambra,’ Momodu Dismisses Soludo’s Victory Promise For Tinubu
item.description: A chieftain of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Dele Momodu, has dismissed Anambra State Governor Chukwuma Soludo’s prediction that President Bola Tinubu will win the 2027 presidential election, insisting that Peter Obi will defeat the President in the state. Momodu, the Deputy Director-General of Media and Communications of the ADC Presidential Campaign Council, said Obi would defeat Soludo “spectacularly” during the election. “With due respect to Prof. (Soludo), he has joined those people I said were speaking like robots about Tinubu. “I guarantee you that Peter Obi will disgrace him spectacularly during the election,” he said. The former Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) presidential aspirant made the remarks on Thursday while appearing on Channels Television’s Politics Today . Asked whether Obi could win Anambra despite Soludo and former governor Chris Ngige supporting Tinubu, and whether he had seen the crowd at the APC rally in the state, Momodu dismissed the significance of the gathering. “It’s good to see the crowd, but I am telling you they are beginning to nauseate Nigerians, and that is why Nigerians are shouting ‘bamayi, bamayi’,” he said. He also claimed that criticism of Tinubu was growing, with leaders increasingly expressing their dissatisfaction with the president. On the APC’s campaign activities across the country, Momodu argued that the ruling party’s extensive mobilisation reflected its concerns about the outcome of the election. “The only reason they are going everywhere feverishly is because they know they will lose the election. I am 66-plus. I have never seen this kind of campaign where the President is beginning to sound like an opposition leader,” he said. Momodu also accused Tinubu of treating APC governors like “robots,” alleging that their public statements appeared coordinated. “I monitored each of the governors. Let me tell you emphatically that they are being treated like robots. There is no question about it,” he said. ﻿ Soludo had earlier on Thursday declared that Tinubu did not need to rig the 2027 election because his administration’s performance would secure his re-election. “To our people, this election, to the best of our knowledge, is already won and lost. The President doesn’t need to rig the election. President Tinubu doesn’t need to rig the election. “All over the country today, in every state of Nigeria, it is President Tinubu and Shetima’s ticket versus one other party. Whereas you have some other candidates who are strong in some parts of the country but don’t exist in others,” he said at an APC presidential campaign rally in Anambra State attended by top party chieftains. item.title: 2027: People Are Rejecting Tinubu, They Can Feel The Pain — Dele Momodu
item.description: A chieftain of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Dele Momodu, says Nigerians are rejecting President Bola Tinubu because they are feeling the adverse impact of his administration’s economic policies. Momodu, who is the Deputy Director-General of Media and Communications of the ADC presidential campaign council, said the growing public discontent was a reflection of the hardship Nigerians have endured since the removal of the fuel subsidy. The former Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) presidential aspirant made the remarks on Thursday while appearing as a guest on Channels Television’s Politics Today. A combo of Dele Momodu and President Bola Tinubu Momodu said the government should have carefully considered the advantages and disadvantages of the policy before implementing it. He likened the country’s economic situation to a patient who had been given an injection and remained in a coma for almost four years. “That’s what is happening in Nigeria. And that is why you can see that everywhere Tinubu goes now, he is being rejected by the people. The people are not stupid; they are rejecting him because they can feel the pain,” he said. ﻿ The publisher accused the President of insensitivity to Nigerians’ economic hardship, citing excessive government spending, inadequate funding of critical sectors and the burden of subsidy removal. “We’ve since discovered that this subsidy issue could have been better handled because, if you look at it, the people who are at fault are probably less than 1,000 people, and now you are punishing over 200 million Nigerians because of the sins of a few people. “If he were sharing in the pain of the people, he would not be doing what he is doing, donating one billion, doing a budget to individuals, a budget in trillions, more than what you are paying the military, more than what you are using to service the health sector, more than what you are spending on the education of our children,” Momodu said. Momodu accused the Tinubu administration of covertly reinstating fuel subsidies and dismissed positive economic assessments by the World Bank and IMF, arguing that they had not improved Nigerians’ living conditions. “The world is praising us; the World Bank is praising us; the IMF is saying we are doing well. Whenever the IMF or World Bank is interested in your case, then something is wrong. You can see clearly that everything you can say is not affecting our people positively. Nigerians are suffering, and that’s just the truth,” he said. Subsidy Removal, ‘Bamayi’ ﻿ Tinubu announced the removal of the fuel subsidy during his inauguration on May 29, 2023, citing its growing cost to government finances. Since that announcement, the policy, alongside the unification of the foreign exchange market, has contributed to higher petrol prices and increased living costs for Nigerians. item.title: Yiaga Africa Urges INEC To Publish Guidelines For Nov. 28 Mock Accreditation
item.description: Yiaga Africa has urged the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to publish comprehensive guidelines and the list of participating polling units for its nationwide mock accreditation and electronic results upload exercise scheduled for November 28. The organisation said timely access to information about the exercise was necessary to enable citizens, political parties, civil society organisations, election observers, and the media to understand, participate in, and monitor the process. In a statement signed by its Executive Director, Samson Itodo, Yiaga Africa welcomed INEC’s decision to conduct the exercise ahead of the 2027 general elections. It said the exercise was consistent with sustained calls by citizens and civil society organisations for the commission to adequately test the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) and the INEC Result Viewing Portal (IReV) before the elections. COMBO: Photo of YIAGA Africa executive director Samson Itodo and INEC Chairman Joash Amupitan “However, Yiaga Africa is concerned that, despite the importance of the exercise, the Commission is yet to make public comprehensive guidelines and a framework outlining how it will be conducted. The list of polling units where the exercise will take place is also yet to be made public. “For an exercise of this significance, timely access to information is essential. Citizens and electoral stakeholders should have sufficient information and notice to understand, participate in, and observe the process,” the statement read in part. Yiaga Africa said transparency in the exercise would be crucial to building public confidence in the electoral technologies that would be deployed for the 2027 elections. It called on INEC to immediately publish a comprehensive framework outlining the scope, modalities and procedures for the exercise. The organisation also urged the commission to release the complete list of participating polling units and other relevant locations early enough to give stakeholders sufficient time to prepare for the exercise. Yiaga Africa further urged INEC to use the mock exercise as an opportunity to demonstrate transparency and responsiveness while allowing meaningful public scrutiny of BVAS and IReV. Last week, INEC had announced November 28 as the date for the nationwide mock accreditation exercise to test its voter accreditation and electronic results transmission systems ahead of the 2027 general elections. The commission’s chairman, Joash Amupitan, said the exercise would simulate the presidential election and take place across all states of the federation. He said the exercise was part of measures to address technical challenges experienced during the 2023 general elections and strengthen the credibility of the 2027 polls. The 2027 Presidential and National Assembly elections are scheduled for January 16, while the governorship and State Houses of Assembly elections will be held on February 6. item.title: When Ndigbo Become President, It Must Be Eight Full Years — Oshiomhole
item.description: Senator representing Edo North, Adams Oshiomhole, has said the South-East should have a full eight-year presidential tenure when a candidate from the region eventually becomes Nigeria’s president. The former Edo State governor spoke on Thursday at an All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign rally in Anambra State, where he endorsed President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid. “When Ndigbo will become president, it must be eight full years. No half-talk. It will be full talk by those with brains, with courage, and fill the gap,” he said. Oshiomhole also praised Anambra State Governor Charles Soludo, a former governor of the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN), for his economic expertise and leadership. ﻿ He said Soludo understood the challenges facing Nigeria’s economy, particularly the disconnect between monetary and fiscal policies. Earlier, Soludo declared that President Tinubu does not need to rig the 2027 presidential election to secure victory, arguing that the President’s performance will earn him another term. “The President doesn’t need to rig the election. President Tinubu doesn’t need to rig the election. President Tinubu and Shettima, they are doing very well. They will win because they have done well,” the governor said. Senator Oshiomhole’s comments on an eight-year presidential tenure for an eventual Igbo president come amid discussions about political power rotation and the South-East’s quest for the presidency. Igbo Presidency, Obi’s Stance Peter Obi speaking at NDC Town Hall meeting in Lagos. Photo: Nosakhale Akhimien/ChannelsTV Former Anambra State governor Peter Obi, who contested the 2023 presidential election, is seeking the nation’s top job again in 2027 under the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), with former Kano State Governor Rabiu Kwankwaso as his running mate. Obi, a South-Easterner, finished third in the 2023 presidential election with 6,101,533 votes, and has pledged to serve only one four-year term if elected, promising to hand over power to the North in 2031. ﻿ He has argued that a single term would allow him to focus on governance without the distractions of seeking re-election. He maintains that 48 months is enough time to tackle insecurity, fix the economy, and stabilise the country. However, the pledge has drawn criticism from some South-East political leaders, who believe the region should not concede a full eight-year presidential tenure.
